subject: Technical deep-dive recap: latency & throughput SLOs
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>

Subject: Technical deep-dive recap: latency & throughput SLOs

Hi Alex / Priya —

Thanks again for the call today — appreciate the deep context on the product flows and where latency spikes are hurting conversion. Below is a short recap of what we heard, the goals you stated, and our recommended Redwood deployment/operational approach ahead of a formal technical deep-dive (we can use this as the agenda).

Summary of pain points / goals
- Primary pain: p99 tail latency during peak on short assistant prompts (search+generation) causing timeouts in the client and degraded UX.
- Secondary: cost per 1k requests is high given current over-provisioning and lack of request-level caching.
- Goals: p95 < 120ms, p99 < 350ms for prompts up to ~512 tokens; sustain 50-75 req/s peak with spikes to 200 req/s for short prompts; keep token cost within current budget or show clear TCO improvement.

Model & workload notes from call
- Main model target: open-weights 70B variant (we discussed quantized 4-bit runtime for production).
- Typical prompt length: 50-120 tokens; generation length usually 20-150 tokens.
- Mix: ~70% short queries (1-2 turns), 30% multi-turn sessions that rely on KV cache reuse.

Recommended Redwood deployment topology (prelim)
- Dedicated regional pool (us-west) of mixed-instance GPUs (H100 for peak throughput, A10G for baseline) with an autoscaling headroom policy to burst to reserved capacity.
- Frontline routing: route short prompt traffic to a low-latency, small-batch fast-path (quantized model variant) and route longer sessions to a high-memory variant to preserve quality.
- KV/prefix caching: enable request-level KV caching for session reuse to reduce repeated compute on multi-turn flows.
- Batching & inference settings: continuous batching target 8-16 for short prompts, 32-48 for longer sequential workloads depending on latency envelope; dynamic batching with capped latency SLOs.
- Fallbacks: A/B fallback to a smaller 13B quantized variant for extreme load or degraded hardware — we can gate this with quality thresholds.

Operational considerations / metrics to collect
- Capture p50/p95/p99 for request latency, plus tail tokens/sec per GPU, queue depth, and cold-start counts.
- Provide a 48-hour sample of production traffic (anonymized) with representative prompt lengths and concurrency to help tune kernels and batching.

Attachments shared
- acme-infra-sketch.png (simple topology sketch)
- redwood-sla-matrix.pdf (SLO mapping & suggested thresholds)

Proposed next steps
1) Share anonymized traffic sample & a short test suite (we can use it to run a canary).
2) Schedule a 60-90 minute technical deep-dive with your infra/ML-engineering + our runtime team — suggested slots next week.
3) We'll produce an initial deployment estimate (cost/throughput/latency) and a suggested rollback/fallback runbook.

If that all looks good I'll send a calendar invite for the deep-dive and loop in our infra lead (Dev) and applied ML (Neha).

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com | (415) 555-0198

Thanks Marissa — this is a great summary. A few quick clarifications before we lock a time: 

- Confirming SLO targets: p95 < 120ms and p99 < 350ms for prompts up to ~512 tokens, correct? Our current p99 is closer to 900ms under peak.
- Model fallback: When you say "A/B fallback to 13B" — is that automatic routing on overloaded capacity or a manual canary? We'd prefer automated fallback with traffic-splitting control.
- GPU options: H100 sounds right for the big batches; what's the baseline per-request cost difference between A10G and H100 for the quantized 70B runtime?

I'll upload a small sample of recent traffic (anonymized) — attaching acme-load-sample.csv. Also, Priya will join the deep-dive from infra.

Adding a few engineering notes ahead of the deep-dive — I want to make sure we have concrete numbers to size GPU and memory: 

- Kernel & memory estimates (rough) for quantized 70B (4-bit)
  - Model weights (4-bit): ~70B * 4 / 8 = ~35GB logical; with activation buffers and KV cache expect ~70-110GB memory requirement per model replica depending on sequence length.
  - For short prompts (<=128 tokens) we can use a small-batch fast-path and keep activation working set lower; recommend 80GB GPU (H100 80GB) for headroom at peak.

- Throughput/latency guidance (empirical starting point)
  - Single H100 80GB running quantized 70B fast-path: ~50-80 short-prompt requests/s at p95 <= 120ms with continuous batching (depends on prompt len).
  - A10G baseline: good for lower-cost steady traffic, roughly 30-40 req/s for short prompts at ~p95 150-220ms.

- KV cache sizing
  - Average session KV size: ~10-20 tokens per turn x average turns; estimate 1.5-3MB per active session in memory for large models. Plan for session sharding across replicas.

- Warm-up & canary plan
  - Pre-warm critical replicas with representative short prompts to populate KV; run a 30-min canary against 5% of traffic before full cutover.

I can come prepared with a simple cost/throughput matrix for H100 vs A10G for the exact traffic sample you share.
